episode_title: 506 The Blueprint of Water: Understanding the Why with Connor Hanrahan, Part 2

real_qa.q: What are the limitations of using AI to edit technical water treatment reports and inspection reports?
real_qa.r: Connor found that AI editing changed his writing voice and how he explained concepts, making reports sound inauthentic and requiring him to undo the changes. He also warns that AI can misrepresent or misdiagnose water treatment issues—for example, providing incorrect recommendations about calcium maintenance in cooling towers running on soft water. The key risk is that customers hire professionals for their expertise and experience, not for how a computer interprets problems.
real_qa.requete: AI editing water treatment reports problems

real_qa.q: How should water professionals use AI as a tool without replacing their professional judgment?
real_qa.r: Connor recommends using AI to generate starting ideas and provide inspiration, but only after filtering through professional experience to determine what actually happens in the field. He also finds AI valuable for consuming and interpreting data—such as reviewing hundreds of monthly reports to flag issues—rather than for generating original technical content. The critical step is evaluating AI output against real-world field knowledge.
real_qa.requete: AI tool water treatment professional judgment

real_qa.q: Why did AI fail to generate an accurate product formulation when Connor asked it to create a treatment chemical solution?
real_qa.r: When Connor input the RAS he planned to use, the customer problems, and requested an order of addition with actives calculations, AI produced a report that was completely incorrect—it would have created an insoluble clump of solution or scale inside the treatment chemical. Connor determined from experience that the components would never dissolve together, and every recommendation in the AI output was wrong from the first paragraph onward.
real_qa.requete: AI chemical formulation product development failure

real_qa.q: What is the bullshit asymmetry paradox and how does it affect water treatment professionals receiving AI-generated advice?
real_qa.r: The bullshit asymmetry paradox describes how it takes ten times more effort to counter false information than to put it out in the first place. Connor encountered customers who received AI-generated recommendations containing incorrect treatment parameters—such as advice about calcium maintenance for scaling prevention in cooling towers running on soft water—and had to spend significant time writing detailed technical rebuttals to correct these false claims.
real_qa.requete: bullshit asymmetry paradox water treatment misinformation

real_qa.q: Why is writing skill underappreciated in the water treatment industry despite its importance?
real_qa.r: Connor explains that technical professionals write many emails and reports daily, but the ability to translate complex information into understandable formats—especially for customers who aren't water treaters—is critically important yet underappreciated. People notice good writing when they see it, but most don't recognize how foundational it is to professional communication in the water treatment field.
real_qa.requete: writing skills water treatment professionals communication
